You build ONE commit of a fine-grained, prototype-first review series for the vsim_andesim repo. The series re-synthesizes 46 messy commits into 50 clean ones. The organizing rule: each functionality is built up in TWO steps -- a MINIMAL prototype commit (smallest real slice, e.g. transport only f0) with its test, then a COMPLETION commit (the rest, f1..f31) with its test. Some commits are single (atomic). Your commit's spec entry has a "slice" field: minimal | completion | single.

WORKSPACE
- Work ONLY in worktree /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/vsim (branch review/vsim-series). NEVER modify /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim's main checkout or other worktrees; read-only git against /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim is fine ('git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/vsim show <sha>' reaches all history).
- NEVER 'git push'. Only branch review/vsim-series.
- Start: 'git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/vsim status --short' clean. End: EXACTLY ONE new commit, clean status.

SPEC
- Read /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/vsim_series_v2.json. Find your entry by id. Also read top-level abi_pins, legacy_never_add, expected_delta_vs_old_tip. Substitute /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad for any SCRATCH in the text; abi/vN checkouts live at /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/abi/v2..v6.

SLICE SEMANTICS (critical -- this is what makes the series reviewable)
- slice=minimal: the code genuinely does ONLY the small slice. E.g. for "GPR restore, min (x1)", the restore writes ONLY x1 (not a loop over x1..x31); the test checks ONLY x1. You author a genuinely reduced version of the final file -- NOT the final file. For X-macro CSR blocks, the minimal commit HAND-CODES the one named CSR (e.g. mxstatus), and the completion commit swaps in the HYBRID_*_CSR_LIST loop.
- slice=completion: expand the previous minimal slice to the full final form (the loop / full list / all registers) and extend the test to cover all. After a completion commit, the touched file should match its final form MINUS features that land in still-later commits.
- slice=single: author the file to final form minus later-feature parts, per construct.
- The construct field tells you exactly what reduced/full content to write and how to derive it from the final file ('git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/vsim show qemu-isa-match:<path>'). Historical commits are reference only; the final file has the fixed form.

BUILD-ORDER FACTS you must honor (ABI symbols/macros only exist after their pin commit):
- hybrid_andes_csr + HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST: only after the v3 pin. hybrid_m_ext_csr + HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST: only after v4. hybrid_l2c: only after v5. write_mask.h: only after v6. Do NOT reference a macro/struct that its pin has not introduced yet -- defer that branch to the commit the spec assigns it to.
- andes_caps.hpp is CREATED partway through: earlier commits that reference it in FINAL must STRIP the include + the caps_ member and reduced call sites, adding them at the caps commit. Follow the construct.
- Tolerant CSR writes evolve: plain write, then caps-gated, then baseline-gated, then write-mask-gated. Each later commit rewraps the same call sites -- do only what YOUR commit's construct says.
- HybridConfig.cmake: every commit that ADDS a tests/hybrid/*.test.cpp must also register it there (per construct).
- NEVER introduce a legacy_never_add item (dead consts, regno_vector, pcs_of_kind/empty, trigger() accessor, --hybrid-enter-pc, any PB register/CSR sweep, stale csrwi-0x7C0 / 'CSR sweep' wording). Write correct wording from day one.

VALIDATION (must pass before committing)
- Run every validate item in your spec entry. Header-only unit tests compile+run from the worktree:
    g++ -std=c++20 -I /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/abi/vN -I /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external/doctest/doctest -I /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/vsim/src <test file> -o /tmp/claude-1002/vtest_${RANDOM} && that binary
  where vN is the ABI pin in effect at your commit (spec 'abi' field / abi_pins). SystemC-linked tests (shared_mem_smoke/offset, memory_map) may be skipped with a note.
- If validation cannot pass, DO NOT commit broken: fix construction, or return status=blocked with precise detail.

GITLINK: to (re)pin external/andesim_abi: git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/vsim update-index --add --cacheinfo 160000,<full sha>,external/andesim_abi

COMMIT MESSAGE: first line = spec subject verbatim. Blank line. Body = 2-6 full sentences from body_points (what + why; note "minimal: only <slice>" or "completes <feature>" so a reviewer sees the step). End with exactly:

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. - verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
